solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Service good or grand here? A state!

parts.note: G, short for good or for grand, sits in the middle of the word night, so mid-night is where it is found
Mass. is the abbreviation for Massachusetts, a US state

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a church service here is good or grand, and is told it is quite a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A state!' looks like an exclamation about a mess, but it is the abbreviated US state. The first half is a riddle: G is what you find at mid-night.
explanation.definitionFit: Midnight Mass is the Christmas Eve church service held at twelve o'clock at night.

clue.text: Film about mad cow disease, all ending in Ohio, say

indicators.note: the word for film goes around the other letters, surrounding them

parts.note: a film is a thin haze or coating, as is a mist

indicators.note: asks for the final letter of every one of the preceding words

parts.note: the last letters of mad, cow and disease

explanation.surface: A documentary about BSE, the cattle illness, ends up being made in Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests a movie, but here it means a misty haze. 'Ohio, say' defines by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohio is one example of a state in the American Midwest region.

clue.text: Old musician woozy, measure of drink found slightly lacking

indicators.note: falling a little short means the word loses just its final letter

parts.note: woozy and dizzy both mean light-headed
a gill is a small liquid measure, a quarter pint
espied means spotted or discovered

explanation.surface: An elderly performer is unsteady after a drink was spotted being slightly short-measured.
explanation.walkthrough: ESPIED loses its last letter. Dizzy Gillespie was a famous American jazz trumpeter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dizzy Gillespie, the bebop trumpeter, died in 1993, so he is a musician of the past.

clue.text: Moonlight in Nice somewhat uplifting, don't you agree, mate?

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up means the letters are read from bottom to top
only part of the run of words is wanted, so the letters sit inside them

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of moonlight, in, and the start of Nice

explanation.surface: Someone enthuses about how uplifting the moonlight is on the French Riviera, seeking a friend's agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: Innit is British slang, a clipped 'isn't it?', used as a tag asking for agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Innit is a colloquial tag question meaning isn't it, so it seeks a friend's agreement.

clue.text: Iberian, say: what had him in a funk?

parts.note: what belonged to him is his
to be in a funk is to be in a state of fear

explanation.surface: Someone asks what made a Spanish man so frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the wordplay asks what gripped him: his panic.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iberian, from Spain or Portugal, is an example of someone of Hispanic origin.

clue.text: Queen sees king hiding in tree

indicators.note: the tree conceals the king within itself, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: may is the hawthorn tree
R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Like Charles II after Worcester, a king hides in a tree while the queen watches.
explanation.walkthrough: May is another name for hawthorn, a hedge tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Several queens of England and Scotland have borne the name, including Mary Tudor and Mary, Queen of Scots.

clue.text: US city offering boat trip round Lapland, might you say?

indicators.note: asks how the phrase sounds when spoken rather than how it is written

parts.note: Lapland is where Father Christmas lives, so a sea journey around it would be his voyage

explanation.surface: An American city is advertising sailing holidays around the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: Lapland, in the far north of Finland, is promoted as Santa Claus's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Cruz is a coastal city in California.

clue.text: Splashing American, swimmer from Mississippi?

parts.note: Jackson is the state capital of Mississippi
the pollock is a fish, so a swimmer in crossword terms

explanation.surface: An American paddling about, a strong swimmer who hails from Mississippi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Splashing' sounds like water play; it is his drip-and-splash painting technique. The fish comes after the state's capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Jackson Pollock was the American abstract painter famous for splashing and dripping paint onto canvas.

clue.text: Moment of truth — for the crisp eater?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the decisive point when things come to a head
second meaning: the noise and bite a person eating potato chips enjoys

explanation.walkthrough: Crisps are what Americans call potato chips; the second half is a playful description of the sound and bite they give.
explanation.definitionFit: When it comes to the crunch is an idiom for the critical point; it is also the crackling bite of crisp food.

clue.text: Practise meditation perhaps every month, for example

parts.note: to do an activity is to practise it
Zen is a school of Buddhism centred on meditation

explanation.surface: Advice to take up meditation, maybe once a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every month' looks like a schedule, but it is the whole set of months in a year.
explanation.definitionFit: There are twelve months in a year, so all of them together make a set of twelve.

clue.text: Back turned on beach, briefly, in Scottish town

indicators.note: kept short, the word for shore drops its final letter

parts.note: a strand is a shore or beach

indicators.note: turned round, so the word for behind is read in the other direction

parts.note: the back is the rear

explanation.surface: Someone lies briefly on the sand, back to the sun, in a Scottish seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed rear is placed after the shortened strand, as 'on' suggests in an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranraer is a port town in Dumfries and Galloway, south-west Scotland.

clue.text: A pity gent cut off from part of Africa

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged
cut short, the word for a gentleman loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: It's a shame a gentleman has been isolated in some region of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut off' reads as a single phrase meaning stranded, but it splits into two signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Egyptian is the adjective for something belonging to Egypt, a country in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Drop off family's cleaner

parts.note: to drop off is to fall asleep, briefly to nap
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A family's cleaner dozes off on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, joining wordplay to definition; 'cleaner' is a thing that wipes, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A napkin is used at table to wipe the mouth and fingers, so it is something that cleans.

clue.text: Uncontrolled descent of alpinist taking a tumble

indicators.note: a tumble throws things into disorder, so the letters fall into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mountaineer falls and slides helplessly down the slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailspin is the spiralling, out-of-control dive of an aircraft, and figuratively any rapid decline.

clue.text: First of suitors snubbin' a young girl

indicators.note: asks for only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the opening letter of suitors
snubbing means ignoring; the apostrophe shows the final G is dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman coldly brushes off the men courting her.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped G in snubbin' signals the same clipped ending on its synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Signorina is Italian for an unmarried young woman, the equivalent of miss.

clue.text: In conversation, mention accessory

indicators.note: signals that the word is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: to broach a subject is to raise or mention it

explanation.surface: Someone casually brings up a fashion accessory while chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: A brooch is an ornamental pin worn on clothing, a kind of jewellery accessory.

clue.text: Indonesian business protected by foundation

indicators.note: something protected is enclosed and shielded by what surrounds it

parts.note: a base is a foundation
one's line is one's trade or line of business

explanation.surface: A company in Indonesia is shielded by a charitable trust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foundation' suggests a charitable body; it is the bottom layer of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an island province of Indonesia, so a Balinese person or thing is Indonesian.

clue.text: Evil country garden evacuated

parts.note: Mali is a West African country

indicators.note: emptied of its contents, so only the outside letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of garden

explanation.surface: A wicked regime clears people out of a country's gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Malign as an adjective means harmful or malevolent, a near synonym of wicked.

clue.text: Doctor, one brought into wine region where the last couple sent spinning

indicators.text: where the last couple sent spinning
indicators.note: only the final pair of letters is spun round, so just those two swap their order
something brought into a place is put inside it

parts.note: the Médoc is a wine district of Bordeaux
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A doctor is taken to a vineyard area where the last two visitors get dizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: The I goes after MED, giving MEDIOC; then only the last two letters are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Medico is an informal word for a physician or medical student.

clue.text: An arm casually wrapped round American love, sweet thing

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are wrapped around the other part, enclosing it
done casually means arranged carelessly, so the letters are shuffled loosely

parts.note: taken as written
zip is American slang for nothing, and love is zero in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone drapes an arm around their American sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet thing' sounds like a term of endearment, but it is a confection.
explanation.definitionFit: Marzipan is a sweet paste of ground almonds and sugar, a confection.

clue.text: Gas worried baby

parts.note: neon is a noble gas
ate, as in what's eating you, means worried or troubled

explanation.surface: A baby with wind is fretting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' and 'worried' look like a colicky infant's symptoms.
explanation.definitionFit: A neonate is a newborn infant, the medical term for a baby in its first weeks.

clue.text: Tyrant, son punching revolutionary was a drunkard

indicators.note: revolving turns things round, so the word is read backwards
a punch goes into something, so this letter is driven inside

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A dictator's son lashes out at a rebel who was once a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun for a rebel; it signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler who wields power cruelly, much like a tyrant.

clue.text: Old boy back tucking into wine and curry

indicators.note: something tucked into another is placed inside it

parts.note: vino is informal for wine
O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: going back means the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A former schoolboy returns home and tucks into wine and a curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old boy' reads as a former pupil, but splits into two pieces that turn round inside VINO.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindaloo is a fiery Indian curry dish of Goan origin.

clue.text: Tot put on a performance

parts.note: a tot and a dram are both a small measure of spirits
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small child put on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' suggests a toddler, but it is a nip of whisky. 'Put on' sets the first piece above the second in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play, so the word can stand for a theatrical performance.

clue.text: Second little creature? That's right!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a moment, as in just a ...
second meaning: a small blood-sucking parasite
third meaning: the mark a teacher puts beside a correct answer

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings. In Britain a check mark is called this, and 'in a ...' means in a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves for an instant of time, a parasitic arachnid, and the mark that signals a correct answer.

clue.text: Trash in cities I tidied up, cleaner on the outskirts earlier

indicators.note: placed earlier means this piece goes in front of the other
the outskirts are the edges, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of cleaner

indicators.note: tidying rearranges things, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rubbish on city streets is cleared up, with a street cleaner working the suburbs first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trash' looks like rubbish, a noun; it is the verb to slate.
explanation.definitionFit: To trash something is slang for slating it harshly, the same as finding fault with it.

clue.text: Island salutation reversing a greeting on Majorca?

indicators.note: reversing means running the letters in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
hola is Spanish for hello, and Majorca is a Spanish island

explanation.surface: A Hawaiian greeting turns out to be a Spanish one said backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloha is the Hawaiian word used for hello and goodbye, so a greeting from those islands.

clue.text: Hand-held device showing western, old film featuring boozer

indicators.note: a film featuring someone has them included within it

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for western
a talkie was an early film with sound
an alkie is slang for an alcoholic

explanation.surface: A portable gadget plays an old cowboy picture about a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' could be a British pub; here it is the person drinking. The drinker goes between W and TALKIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkie-talkie is a portable two-way radio carried in the hand.
